posts.caption:
iPhone: yes. Android: nearly.

Here is exactly where we are, because we would rather tell you than let you guess.

EffePadelle is live on the App Store. If you have an iPhone you can download it today, for free, and have a competition running tonight. That part is finished and it is real.

Android is a different queue. The app is built, it is tested, and it has been submitted to the Google Play Store. It is now in review, which means a team at Google is checking it against their rules before they let it through. We cannot speed that up and we cannot skip it. Every app goes through the same door.

What we can tell you is that nothing is wrong. There is no bug holding it back, no rejection to fix, no rebuild waiting to happen. It is simply waiting its turn, and that turn takes as long as it takes.

The moment it clears, two things happen at once. The app appears in the Play Store and anyone on Android can download it that same day. And this page starts properly: every week one thing the app actually does, shown instead of described. How a competition gets made in about a minute. How the rounds plan themselves so nobody has to chase anybody. How the table keeps itself. How eight people with four different schedules still end up on a court together.

Until then it stays quiet here. We would rather post nothing than post filler.

If you play padel with roughly the same group and it falls apart somewhere between February and March, this is the app for that. Not for finding strangers. For keeping the people you already like playing together, with a season instead of a group chat.

Follow along if you want to be here when it opens.

iPhone: link in bio.
Android: any day now.
